Matched. D027 announces NVIDIA Spectrum-X, an accelerated networking platform for AI. previous_disclosures.summary: Compute & Networking revenue increased year-on-year, driven by a 266% growth in Compute due to higher shipments of the NVIDIA Hopper GPU computing platform for LLMs, recommendation engines, and generative AI applications, as well as a 133% increase in Networking due to higher InfiniBand shipments.

current_disclosures.section: Results of Operations > Operating Income by Reportable Segments
current_disclosures.summary: Compute & Networking revenue increased year-over-year due to strong demand for accelerated computing and AI solutions. Data Center computing revenue grew 162% driven by the Hopper computing platform for large language models and generative AI, while Data Center networking revenue grew 51% driven by Ethernet for AI and the Spectrum-X end-to-end ethernet platform.

materiality_analysis.reason: The 2025 disclosure explicitly identifies Spectrum-X as a specific driver of the 51% growth in Data Center networking revenue, whereas the 2024 disclosure only announced its introduction. This represents a material update to the company's business performance, confirming the commercial adoption and financial impact of this specific strategic product platform.

comparisons.peer_topic: R&D Expense Increase and AI Headcount
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's research and development expenses increased by 10% to $6.5 billion in 2024, primarily driven by higher employee-related costs resulting from an increase in headcount to support the company's AI strategy.
comparisons.comparison: While both companies disclose investments in AI, NVDA highlights a specific product announcement for its AI networking platform, whereas AMD discloses financial metrics related to the cost of supporting its AI strategy. NVDA announces 'NVIDIA Spectrum-X, an accelerated networking platform for AI,' indicating a product-level focus on data center infrastructure. In contrast, AMD reports that 'Research and development expenses of $6.5 billion in 2024 increased by $584 million, or 10%, compared to $5.9 billion in 2023,' with the increase attributed to 'higher employee-related costs due to an increase in headcount in support of our AI strategy.' NVDA's disclosure focuses on a specific technological solution (Spectrum-X), while AMD's focuses on the broader financial implication (R&D spending) of building out its AI capabilities.

sentences.text: We announced NVIDIA Spectrum-X, an accelerated networking platform for AI.
Research and development expenses of $6.5 billion in 2024 increased by $584 million, or 10%, compared to $5.9 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily due to higher employee-related costs due to an increase in headcount in support of our AI strategy.
